title: Byte Bit Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Bits and Bytes
Bitwise Operators
Hexadecimal
MSB and LSB
Bit Ordering
description: Toggle the eight bits of a byte, apply set, clear and shift operations, predict the result, and watch the byte go onto a wire MSB-first or LSB-first.

learningObjectives: Apply set, clear and shift operations to a byte and state the new value
Convert a byte between decimal, hexadecimal and binary
Predict the order in which bits appear on the wire for MSB-first and LSB-first

keyQuestions: Why does shifting left multiply by 2?
What happens to bit 0 when you shift right?
Which bit goes on the wire first in MSB-first order?
commonMisconceptions: Bit 1 is the rightmost bit (bits are numbered from 0, so the rightmost is bit 0)
LSB-first sends a different value (it sends the same bits in the opposite order)
assessmentOpportunities: The student predicts that shift left doubles the value until bit 7 falls off.
The student writes the Python expression to set or clear a given bit.
The student explains why sender and receiver must agree on bit order.
